stem: Which component of the PHACE syndrome mnemonic refers to posterior fossa abnormalities?
explanation: Posterior fossa anomalies are the correct component of the PHACE syndrome mnemonic. The P in PHACE refers to posterior fossa anomalies, which include malformations such as Dandy-Walker malformation.
rationale: The mnemonic PHACE includes posterior fossa anomalies as one of its defining features.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because hepatic cirrhosis is not part of the PHACE mnemonic.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the P in PHACE stands for posterior fossa anomalies.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because abdominal wall defects are not included in PHACE; the A stands for arterial anomalies.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because endocrine dysfunction is not part of the PHACE mnemonic; the E relates to eye abnormalities.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because cardiac defects are not part of the PHACE acronym.

source.hint: This letter in the mnemonic refers to brain malformations, specifically in the back part of the skull.
